distinguishing_features: Geometric profile change (15° tapered trapezoidal seal cross-section) creating a micro-plasto-hydrodynamic wedge, rather than a monitoring/inference scheme
Material held constant (existing NBR), so novelty rests on geometry not substitution
Mechanism actively reduces peak contact stress to prevent fatigue crack initiation, rather than detecting a degradation precursor
Relies on pressure-cycling-induced transient fluid film formation (h_min ≈ 0.67 μm) to avoid asperity contact
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent fatigue crack initiation and leakage in a cyclically pressure-loaded elastomeric seal without changing material or increasing maintenance/operational burden.
parsed.viable_reason: The film-thickness formula is dimensionally inconsistent and misapplied (a numerical coefficient, missing dimensionless groups, and conditions that yield no meaningful 0.67 μm), so the stated 30% stress reduction and asperity-separation claim are unsupported and physically implausible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Employing a tapered wedge geometry to generate a hydrodynamic film in a cyclically loaded seal is a non-routine geometric departure, not a mere parameter tweak of the monitoring-based prior art.
